builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DrugCoding: A Scientific Programming Agent for Drug Discovery
summary: DrugCoding replaces manually orchestrated drug discovery workflows with an LLM agent that plans tasks, routes to specialized scientific models, generates and executes code, and coordinates multi-agent validation. It costs the overhead of maintaining tool interfaces, model routing infrastructure, and multi-agent execution on top of API or local model usage, plus benchmark-specific adaptation. It can fail when scientific tools are misinvoked, when generated code executes incorrectly despite validation, or when the underlying LLM's planning or routing degrades on workflows outside the benchmark distribution.
rationale: The reported gains are tool-calling accuracy on a drug discovery benchmark rather than end-to-end production outcomes, so an engineer should validate the orchestration pattern on their own pipelines and tool stack before adopting it as infrastructure.
technique: Scientific programming agent for drug discovery

claims.statement: DrugCoding replaces manually orchestrated drug discovery workflows with an LLM agent that plans tasks, routes to specialized scientific models, generates and executes code, and coordinates multi-agent validation. It costs the overhead of maintaining tool interfaces, model routing infrastructure, and multi-agent execution on top of API or local model usage, plus benchmark-specific adaptation. It can fail when scientific tools are misinvoked, when generated code executes incorrectly despite validation, or when the underlying LLM's planning or routing degrades on workflows outside the benchmark distribution.

DrugCoding achieves an average session-level Pass@1 of 97.35% on the full benchmark, outperforming the strongest baseline, Codex, by 9.24 percentage points; on the challenging subset it reaches 97.92%.
